name: Anti-intellectualism
summary: Anti-intellectualism is hostility to or mistrust of education, science, philosophy and the arts, and of those who represent them. It dismisses intellectual work as impractical or politically motivated and casts educated elites as out of touch with ordinary people. It shows up in religious, populist and practical-minded forms and is not tied to a single economic program.
scope: The Hofstadter-style account of anti-intellectualism as a populist and practical attitude in modern democracies, mainly American, drawing on Wikipedia's overview, Hofstadter's Anti-Intellectualism in American Life as described by secondary sources, and Woodrow Wilson's 1912 speeches as a documented instance of anti-expert rhetoric. It is an attitude rather than a program, so most economic and social statements are unanswered. It excludes authoritarian purges of intellectuals (Khmer Rouge, for example), which are treated as a separate phenomenon.
